summary: Two celebrated swindlers: Austro-Hungarian grifter Victor Lustig, who ran money-box scams in 1920s America and sold the Eiffel Tower for scrap before dying in federal custody, and Indian con man Natwarlal, who fleeced businessmen and escaped jail for decades.

evidence.note: Lustig born probably in Hostinne, Austria-Hungary, in the 1890s; birthplace unverified
1908 arrests in Prague and Vienna, later cons in Zurich before moving to Paris in 1912
first US arrest in Kansas City in 1918 marks start of his American con career
Lustig and Dapper Dan Collins travel to Paris and plan the Eiffel Tower sale
counterfeit hundred-dollar notes feared to shake confidence in the dollar
bedsheet escape from Manhattan detention, recapture, then Alcatraz
untreated pneumonia, transfer to Missouri prison hospital, death in 1947
Natwarlal born in a Bihar village sometime between 1912 and 1925
villagers treat him as a Robin Hood folk hero and plan a statue
1979 Bollywood film about him cements a largely invented legend
last escape in 1996 at age 84; death year disputed between 1996 and 2009

notes: Part 2 is entirely about Natwarlal, so both men are primary. Natwarlal's birth year is uncertain (1912-1925); 1912 follows his stated age of 84 in 1996. Death is disputed (brother says 1996, lawyer 2009); 1996, his last known sighting, used as lifespan end. Lustig's 1890 birth year comes from general knowledge plus the transcript's age 18 in 1908.
